SB02-q01-q6op89: Students are usually safest on the bus; first recognize the hazard and, if time permits, call your dispatcher before deciding.
The handbook says to contact your dispatcher, not parents, before deciding whether to evacuate.
SB02-q02-ty7hc6: Students are usually safest and easiest to control on the bus, unless staying exposes them to needless risk.
The road shoulder puts students near traffic; the general rule is to keep them on the bus.
SB02-q03-82d92m: Being stalled on or next to a railroad crossing is one of the 5 mandatory evacuations.
A threat of fire is one of the 5 mandatory evacuations.
SB02-q04-o2lgv2: The safe place is at least 100 ft off the road, toward oncoming traffic, so crash debris does not hit students.
300 ft is the HazMat spill distance; a roadside safe place is at least 100 ft off, toward oncoming traffic.
SB02-q05-ct74nr: Downwind puts students in the smoke; lead them upwind so smoke blows away from them.
The handbook says lead students upwind of a burning bus, not to a spot near it.
SB02-q06-9t3xr4: Downwind blows fumes onto students; for HazMat go upwind at least 300 ft. 100 ft is the roadside distance.
Upwind is right, but a HazMat spill needs at least 300 ft; 50 ft is the farthest crossing stop distance.
SB02-q07-r614r7: Move away from the tracks at an angle toward the train, not in the direction the train is going.
Get everyone far from the bus at an angle away from the tracks and toward the train.
SB02-q08-wv7f07: Assign 2 older, responsible students to each exit; 1 more student leads everyone to the safe place.
Plan ahead with 2 older, responsible student helpers per emergency exit, and explain the plan to all students.
SB02-q09-s0vdnv: Do not move a possible neck or spine injury unless life is in immediate danger; special methods are needed.
Carrying still moves the student; don't move a possible neck or spine injury unless life is in immediate danger.
SB02-q10-nj58ii: Flashing red lights make a crossing active; a passive crossing has no traffic control device.
A passive crossing has no traffic control device, so the decision to cross is entirely yours.
SB02-q11-rw5j4d: The X-shaped sign is the crossbuck at the crossing; the advance warning sign is round, black on yellow.
The advance warning sign is round, not diamond-shaped; it is black on yellow.
SB02-q12-8um6wm: 50 ft is the farthest you should stop; stop no closer than 15 ft and no farther than 50 ft.
10 ft is too close; stop no closer than 15 ft and no farther than 50 ft from the nearest rail.
SB02-q13-tmumxy: Turning off radios and noisy equipment and quieting passengers is a required step at the crossing.
Opening the driver's window and looking and listening for a train is a required step at the crossing.
SB02-q14-bi6tt8: Stop only before the first track; when no train is coming on any track, cross them all without stopping.
Never stop between tracks; stop only before the first track, then cross all until completely clear.
SB02-q15-wdwcjb: If the gate comes down after you start across, keep going and drive through it, even if it breaks.
Don't back up; keep going and drive through the gate, even if it breaks.
SB02-q16-ak38kd: Never drive around a gate that stays down after the train passes; call your dispatcher.
The handbook says call your dispatcher when the gate stays down after the train passes.
SB02-q17-qliu6b: Bus length alone is not enough; the rule of thumb is bus length plus 15 ft.
The space depends on your bus: bus length plus 15 ft. 50 ft is the farthest crossing stop distance.
SB02-q18-ocjvns: Never put a student off the bus except at school or at the student's own stop.
If you cannot drive safely, stop in a safe place off the road and call an administrator or the police.
SB02-q19-shzanm: March 1, 1998 is the date for air-brake vehicles; hydraulic-brake buses of 10,000 lb or more use March 1, 1999.
The handbook's ABS dates are March 1, 1998 (air brakes) and March 1, 1999 (hydraulic, 10,000 lb or more).
SB02-q20-xj9uja: Do not pump the brakes in an ABS emergency stop; brake normally and ease off as needed to stay in control.
Brake as you always have, using only the force needed to stop safely and stay in control.
SB02-q21-6b6gsi: 200 ft is where you turn on hazard lights before a crossing; [CA] the strobe limit is 500 ft or less.
[CA] Use the strobe only when fog, rain, snow, smoke or dust cut visibility to 500 ft or less.
SB02-q22-rza5kb: The lookout only warns you; the lookout should not tell you how to back.
You signal for quiet on the bus yourself; the lookout warns of obstacles, people and vehicles.
SB02-q23-dwzre5: At a drop-off point, back first, then unload; loading first is the pick-up point rule.
Never back when students are outside the bus; at a drop-off, back first, then unload.
SB02-q24-tp2g8c: 12 ft is the danger-zone distance; a school bus can have up to 3 ft of tail swing.
Tail swing happens when you turn, up to 3 ft; check your mirrors before and during every turn.
